question: Should ClawRouter support a non-Cloudflare production runtime, and what minimum parity must it guarantee for identity, authoritative policy and budget state, queues, retention, assets, migrations, and operations?
rationale: The request expands supported platform scope across several safety-critical and stateful services, while current repository policy does not establish whether full or reduced non-Cloudflare operation belongs in the product.

options.title: Sponsor portable runtime parity
options.body: Approve provider-neutral service contracts and require the Docker implementation to pass functional, safety, migration, and upgrade parity checks.

options.title: Define a reduced local edition
options.body: Approve a limited self-hosted mode with clearly documented unsupported capabilities and safeguards against treating it as full production parity.

options.title: Keep Cloudflare production-only
options.body: Continue supporting Wrangler local development while retaining Cloudflare as the sole supported production runtime.

recommendation.title: Sponsor portable runtime parity
recommendation.body: Approve provider-neutral service contracts and require the Docker implementation to pass functional, safety, migration, and upgrade parity checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The present runtime, state, and control-plane boundaries primarily derive from their merged architecture work and subsequent ownership of these files.
